summary: Baileys fork: static keyword co-occurrence in utility module, no traced installer harm
details: Package is a fork of the Baileys WhatsApp Web library. A a static rule fired on lib/Utils/generics.js citing keyword co-occurrence of 'ping' and 'GET' tokens, which is consistent with the library's normal WebSocket keep-alive and HTTP helper code rather than a specific exfiltration path. No concrete evidence of installer-secret reads (no ~/.aws, ~/.ssh, ~/.npmrc, env-var scraping), no hardcoded attacker C2 destination, no install/import-time fetch-and-execute, no lifecycle scripts performing network operations, and no traced data-to-destination flow were identified. The package is a lookalike-scope fork of a widely-used library, which alone is not a threat class; behavior in the shipped code does not exhibit a supply-chain attack fingerprint on this record.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
